questions.question: A healthy human heart is divided into how many chambers?
questions.explanation: Two atria sit on top and two ventricles below.

questions.question: Which pair of organs do we use to breathe?
questions.explanation: Air goes in and out of the lungs, where oxygen enters the blood.

questions.question: Damage to which area, usually in the left hemisphere, can leave a person understanding speech but unable to produce fluent words?
questions.explanation: Broca's area is linked to speech production; damage causes a non-fluent aphasia.

questions.question: Which organ mixes food with strong acid and enzymes after you swallow it?
questions.explanation: The stomach churns food and starts breaking down proteins.

questions.question: Which pair of organs filters waste from the blood and makes urine?
questions.explanation: Each kidney filters blood and removes waste and extra water.

questions.question: Which blood cells contain haemoglobin to carry oxygen?
questions.explanation: Red cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen.

questions.question: About how many bones does an adult human have?
questions.explanation: Babies have more, but many bones fuse as we grow, leaving 206 in most adults.

questions.question: Which organ covers the whole body and shields it from germs and injury?
questions.explanation: The skin covers the whole body and protects it from germs, water loss and injury.

questions.question: Why do antibiotics not work against influenza?
choices: Viruses lack the cell structures that antibiotics attack
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial features such as cell walls; viruses have none of those and live inside our cells.

questions.question: Diabetes is a condition that affects the level of what in the blood?
questions.explanation: In diabetes the body cannot keep blood glucose in a healthy range.

questions.question: What does a malignant tumour do that a benign one does not?
choices: Invades nearby tissue and can spread
questions.explanation: Benign tumours stay in place; malignant ones invade and can metastasise.

questions.question: Which blood cells are the main fighters of the immune system?
questions.explanation: White blood cells find and destroy germs.

questions.question: Which insect spreads malaria to people?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes carry the malaria parasite.

questions.question: Roughly which reading is generally considered the upper edge of normal blood pressure for an adult?
questions.explanation: About 120/80 mmHg is the usual healthy target.

questions.question: Cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease and haemophilia are all examples of what kind of illness?
questions.explanation: They are caused by changes in a person's DNA.

questions.question: Which condition makes the airways narrow so that breathing is difficult and wheezy?
questions.explanation: In asthma the airways are inflamed and tighten.

questions.question: Antibiotics are medicines used to treat infections caused by what?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics kill or stop the growth of bacteria.

questions.question: Which kind of vaccine uses a molecule that carries instructions for cells to make a harmless piece of the germ?
questions.explanation: mRNA vaccines deliver instructions so our own cells make an antigen, such as the coronavirus spike protein.

questions.question: Which common medicine is used to reduce fever and mild pain?
questions.explanation: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is widely used for pain and fever.

questions.question: People with type 1 diabetes need regular doses of which medicine?
questions.explanation: Without insulin, glucose cannot enter cells.

questions.question: What is the main job of an anaesthetic in surgery?
questions.explanation: Anaesthetics let operations happen without pain.

questions.question: A lack of which vitamin caused scurvy among sailors on long voyages?
questions.explanation: Fresh fruit and vegetables supply vitamin C.

questions.question: A CT scan builds its images by combining what?
choices: Many X-ray slices taken from different angles
questions.explanation: A rotating X-ray tube and detectors collect slices that a computer assembles into a 3D picture.

questions.question: Which imaging method, using sound waves, is commonly used to look at a baby before birth?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is safe and shows live moving images.

questions.question: A defibrillator is used to treat which emergency?
choices: A chaotic heart rhythm such as ventricular fibrillation
questions.explanation: A controlled shock can reset the heart to a normal rhythm.

questions.question: A surgeon who makes only tiny cuts and uses a camera on a thin tube is doing what kind of surgery?
questions.explanation: Laparoscopic or keyhole surgery means smaller wounds and quicker healing.

questions.question: The Human Genome Project, completed in 2003, was an effort to do what?
choices: Read the full sequence of human DNA
questions.explanation: It determined the order of about three billion DNA base pairs.

questions.question: What is an artificial replacement for a missing arm or leg called?
questions.explanation: Prostheses replace a missing body part.

questions.question: Why must doctors match donors and recipients, and give anti-rejection drugs?
choices: The recipient's immune system may attack the new organ
The new organ would grow too big
questions.explanation: Immunosuppressants reduce the chance that the immune system rejects the foreign tissue.

questions.question: Which instrument do doctors use to listen to heartbeats and breathing?
questions.explanation: The stethoscope amplifies sounds from inside the chest.

questions.question: The word 'vaccine' comes from the Latin word for what animal?
questions.explanation: Jenner used cowpox, and vacca is Latin for cow.

questions.question: Which French scientist showed that many diseases are caused by germs and is remembered in the name of a milk process?
questions.explanation: Pasteurisation uses gentle heat to kill harmful microbes.

questions.question: Which two scientists, with Fleming, shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for penicillin after turning it into a usable drug?
questions.explanation: Florey and Chain led the team that purified penicillin and tested it at Oxford.

questions.question: Washing hands with soap helps prevent what?
questions.explanation: Clean hands remove germs that spread disease.

questions.question: Before Harvey, the Roman physician Galen taught that blood was made in the liver and what?
choices: Used up by the body rather than circulating
questions.explanation: Galen's view held for about 1,400 years until Harvey's experiments.

questions.question: The idea of keeping an operating theatre free of germs is called what?
questions.explanation: Asepsis aims to keep germs out in the first place, going further than antiseptic treatment.
